assertion: The White House Council of Economic Advisers, for example, estimated in October that a plan to extend Medicare benefits to all Americans would cost the federal government $47 trillion over 10 years.
independent_value: CEA report p.4: Medicare for All -47.41 trillion, 2027-2036, constant 2026 dollars

assertion: One recent White House cost estimate pegged the annual price tag at $4.7 trillion.
independent_value: The report states $47.41T over ten years; $4.7T per year is derived by dividing by ten. The report's other $4.7T mentions concern a different calculation (pp. 79, 82).
inaccuracy: Per-year figure is not stated in the report; it is arithmetic

assertion: The panel's estimates place the cost of the plan at $69.7 billion a year starting in 2032.

inaccuracy: Matches the board's most optimistic scenario only

assertion: An analysis commissioned for the state from the Milliman consulting firm found that without changes, total spending on healthcare per year in Oregon would reach at least $76.3 billion by 2032.
independent_value: Milliman status quo 2032: $78.3B best, $72.8B low; $76.3B = low plus $3.5B Part B in the board deck
inaccuracy: Milliman's low case is $72.8B; $76.3B includes Part B added by the board
why_not: The $76.3 figure does appear on deck p.4, but as the board's Part B-adjusted column (72.8 + 3.5), not as Milliman's finding; Milliman's own best estimate is $78.3B.
